content: FAHD1, also referred to as the FLJ36880 protein, is an enzyme in humans encoded by the FAHD1 gene located on chromosome 16. The FAHD1 gene encodes a protein with a molecular weight of 24 kDa, which is localized to the mitochondria. This protein is a member of the fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase family. The structural analysis of FAHD1 at a resolution of 2 Å reveals that its overall structure is similar to the C-terminal domain of the bifunctional enzyme HpcE from Escherichia coli, fumarylacetoacetate hydrolase from Mus musculus (mouse), and YcgM (Apc5008) from E. coli. Several conserved amino acids, including Aspartate-102 (Asp-102) and Arginine-106 (Arg-106), are critical for the catalytic activity of FAHD1. Functionally, FAHD1 has been demonstrated to act as an oxaloacetate decarboxylase in eukaryotic cells. Additionally, it likely functions as an acylpyruvase, as it has been shown to catalyze the hydrolysis of acetylpyruvate and fumarylpyruvate in in vitro experiments. The presence of magnesium ions (Mg²⁺) is essential for achieving maximal enzymatic activity.
